title: Ordinary direct-image and internal-Hom evaluation scalar square
statement:
Let $A\to B$ be a homomorphism of commutative rings and $f:Y\to X$ a morphism of schemes. Work with constant ring sheaves on small etale sites, small in the module universe, and ordinary uncompleted unbounded derived module categories. Write $F_W=-\otimes_A^LB$ for $W=X,Y$, $H_R=R\mathcal Hom_R$ for $R=A,B$, and $\alpha_{R,P}:f_R^*Rf_{*,R}P\to P$ for the ordinary counit. Use the canonical scalar tensor and pullback identifications. Let $L,N\in D(Y_{\mathrm{et}},A)$, let $N'\in D(Y_{\mathrm{et}},B)$, and let $b:F_YN\to N'$ be any morphism, not necessarily invertible. Put $Q=H_A(L,N)$ and $T=Rf_{*,A}Q$.

Define $u:F_YQ\to H_B(F_YL,F_YN)$ as the tensor--Hom transpose of $F_Y(\mathrm{ev}_A)$ under $F_Y(Q\otimes_A^LL)\cong F_YQ\otimes_B^LF_YL$. Define $c_{f,Q}:F_XT\to Rf_{*,B}F_YQ$ to be the $f_B^*\dashv Rf_{*,B}$ adjunct of $F_Y(\alpha_{A,Q})$ under $f_B^*F_X\cong F_Yf_A^*$. Put
$$w=H_B(1,b)\circ u,\qquad h=Rf_{*,B}(w)\circ c_{f,Q}:F_XT\longrightarrow Rf_{*,B}H_B(F_YL,N'),$$
$$e_A=\mathrm{ev}_A\circ(\alpha_{A,Q}\otimes1):f_A^*T\otimes_A^LL\longrightarrow N,$$
and let $\iota:F_Y(f_A^*T\otimes_A^LL)\xrightarrow{\sim}f_B^*F_XT\otimes_B^LF_YL$ be the canonical comparison. The composite ordinary inverse-image and tensor--Hom transpose of $h$ is
$$p_h=\mathrm{ev}_{B,F_YL,N'}\circ\bigl((\alpha_{B,H_B(F_YL,N')}\circ f_B^*h)\otimes1\bigr).$$
Then the following specified equality holds in $D(Y_{\mathrm{et}},B)$:
$$p_h=b\circ F_Y(e_A)\circ\iota^{-1}:f_B^*F_XT\otimes_B^LF_YL\longrightarrow N'.$$
No flatness, finiteness of coefficients, properness of $f$, boundedness, constructibility, exceptional pullback, or invertibility of $u,c_{f,Q},b$ is assumed.

Conventions: [def-pc-scheme], [def-weil-size-convention], [def-weil-pbc-derived-categories], [def-kun-derived-tensor], [lem-pur-derived-change-of-rings], [lem-weil-pbc-ringed-topoi-derived-tensor-pullback], [def-kun-projection-formula-map], [def-pur-derived-internal-hom], [lem-sfb-dc-hom-scalar-adjunction].

proof.text: Write $P_R=f_R^*$, $G_R=Rf_{*,R}$, $F=F_Y$, $a_Z:P_BF_XZ\xrightarrow{\sim}FP_AZ$ for the inverse of the statement's pullback identification, and $\mu_{U,V}:F(U\otimes_A^LV)\xrightarrow{\sim}FU\otimes_B^LFV$. The natural tensor comparison is [lem-weil-pbc-ringed-topoi-derived-tensor-pullback], applied to the identity geometric morphism with structural ring map $A\to B$. The composition/2-isomorphism comparisons of [lem-sfb-ringed-derived-monoidal-comparisons] give the specified $a$: the two ringed-topos factorizations have the same composite structural map. Put $D=P_AT$, $d=\alpha_{A,Q}:D\to Q$, and $H'=H_B(FL,N')$. The canonical comparison in the question is precisely $\iota=(a_T^{-1}\otimes1_{FL})\circ\mu_{D,L}$. All these are comparisons for ordinary derived pullback; neither a direct-image isomorphism nor a completed coefficient comparison is used.

proof.text:
The ordinary derived adjunction with counit $\alpha_B$ is the one specified in [def-kun-projection-formula-map]. The definition of $c=c_{f,Q}$ as adjunct means, by applying the inverse Hom-bijection to that defining equality,
$$t:=\alpha_{B,FQ}\circ P_B(c)=F(d)\circ a_T:P_BF_XT\longrightarrow FQ.$$
This uses only that an adjunction bijection and its inverse cancel. In particular $c$ need not be invertible.

source.place: Proof paragraph 4, comparisons defined by the same adjunction counits; expansion of the ordinary direct-image adjunct

proof.text:
Expand $h=G_B(w)\circ c$ and use functoriality of $P_B$. Naturality of the counit of the adjunction in [def-kun-projection-formula-map], at $w:FQ\to H'$, says
$$\alpha_{B,H'}\circ P_BG_B(w)=w\circ\alpha_{B,FQ}.$$
Consequently
$$\alpha_{B,H'}\circ P_B(h)=w\circ\alpha_{B,FQ}\circ P_B(c)=w\circ t.$$
Every term here is a morphism from $P_BF_XT$ to $H'$ after the displayed precomposition; this is a naturality equation, not a base-change isomorphism assertion.

source.place: Proof paragraph 4, ordinary adjunction counit part of transposing the comparisons

proof.text:
By [lem-sf-ringed-derived-tensor-hom-adjunction], the recorded derived internal Hom $H_B(FL,-)$ is right adjoint to right tensoring by $FL$ for the native derived tensor, which agrees with the K-flat derived tensor through its simultaneous K-flat comparison; this is a closed tensor-Hom structure in the sense of [def-coef-ringed-tensor-hom-model], with evaluation as its counit, natural in the second variable. The tensor-Hom transposes and the evaluations $\mathrm{ev}_A,\mathrm{ev}_B$ of the statement are those of these adjunctions. The defining transpose of $u$ gives
$$\mathrm{ev}_{B,FL,FN}\circ(u\otimes1_{FL})=F(\mathrm{ev}_A)\circ\mu_{Q,L}^{-1}.$$
Naturality of this counit at $b:FN\to N'$ gives
$$\mathrm{ev}_{B,FL,N'}\circ(H_B(1,b)\otimes1_{FL})=b\circ\mathrm{ev}_{B,FL,FN}.$$
Substitution of $w=H_B(1,b)u$, followed by the tensor bifunctor composition law, therefore gives
$$\mathrm{ev}_{B,FL,N'}\circ(w\otimes1_{FL})=b\circ F(\mathrm{ev}_A)\circ\mu_{Q,L}^{-1}.$$
These are the inverse-bijection identity for the specified transpose and naturality of evaluation, so arbitrary $b$ is allowed.

source.place: Proof paragraph 1, definition by tensoring evaluation and transposing; paragraph 4, transposing the comparisons

proof.text:
Apply simultaneous naturality of the tensor comparison [lem-weil-pbc-ringed-topoi-derived-tensor-pullback] to $(d,1_L):(D,L)\to(Q,L)$. It says
$$\mu_{Q,L}\circ F(d\otimes1_L)=(F(d)\otimes1_{FL})\circ\mu_{D,L}.$$
Multiplying by the inverse comparisons gives the needed equality
$$\mu_{Q,L}^{-1}\circ(F(d)\otimes1_{FL})=F(d\otimes1_L)\circ\mu_{D,L}^{-1}.$$
Only the canonical tensor comparisons are inverted; $d$ is not inverted.

Insert Steps 2 and 3 into the definition of $p_h$ and then use Steps 4 and 5. The entire calculation, with composition written right to left, is
$$\begin{aligned}p_h
&=\mathrm{ev}_{B,FL,N'}\circ(w\otimes1)\circ(t\otimes1)\\
&=b\circ F(\mathrm{ev}_A)\circ\mu_{Q,L}^{-1}\circ(F(d)\otimes1)\circ(a_T\otimes1)\\
&=b\circ F(\mathrm{ev}_A)\circ F(d\otimes1)\circ\mu_{D,L}^{-1}\circ(a_T\otimes1)\\
&=b\circ F(e_A)\circ\iota^{-1}.
\end{aligned}$$
The final line uses $e_A=\mathrm{ev}_A(d\otimes1)$, functoriality of $F$, and the inverse of the explicit factorization of $\iota$ in Step 1. Its source is $P_BF_XT\otimes_B^LFL$ and target is $N'$, exactly as required.
